belongs_to: Fig. 8.1: "Observe the following figures and try drawing them freehand." (later: "recreate the images in Fig. 8.1")
description: Fig. 8.1 is one printed figure holding FIVE line drawings (black outlines only, no fill, no labels, no measurements), arranged in three rows. Row 1, left: two equal circles side by side that touch each other at exactly one point (externally tangent, centres on one horizontal line). Row 1, right: two concentric circles (same centre), inner circle about half the diameter of the outer one. Row 2, left: three equal circles in a horizontal row; circle 1 overlaps circle 2 and circle 2 overlaps circle 3 (each overlap is a lens shape, centre-to-centre distance about 0.8 of a diameter); circles 1 and 3 do not meet. Row 2, right: a mouse-like face: one big circle (the head); two ear circles, each about half the diameter of the head, one at the upper left and one at the upper right of the head, each touching the head from outside at a single point; inside the head two small circles (the eyes, each about a quarter of the head diameter) side by side, each holding a small solid black dot at its centre; one small solid black dot (the nose) at the centre of the head, below and midway between the eyes; one short horizontal line segment (the mouth) below the nose, about a third of the head diameter long. Row 3 (centre): two straight line segments forming a big X that cross each other once; each segment starts at an open top end and runs down and outward to touch a small empty circle: the segment going down to the left ends on a small circle at the lower left, the one going down to the right ends on a small circle at the lower right; the two small circles are equal, each about 0.4 of the head-circle diameter, and sit side by side at the same height (like a pair of scissors). Caption "Fig. 8.1" below. Faint watermark and the chapter-opening art / QR code above are not part of the figure.
unclear: No measurements are printed; all relative sizes are read off the picture.

belongs_to: "Do you know what curves are? They are any shapes that can be drawn on paper with a pencil, and include straight lines, circles and other figures as shown below"
description: Five unlabelled hand-style line drawings, in two rows. Top row, left to right: (1) an open wavy curve that starts low at the left, runs right as a gentle S-shape and rises up to the right; (2) a circle; (3) one straight slanting line segment rising to the right. Bottom row, left to right: (4) a closed irregular blob with a wobbly boundary (like a rough pebble outline); (5) an open squiggly curve with one loop (an S-like shape ending in a small rising tail). No numbers, no labels.

belongs_to: "Mark a point P in your notebook. Then, mark as many points as possible ... that are 4 cm away from P." / "You can start by marking a few points of distance 4 cm from P using the compass"

A second dashed segment runs from P up and to the right (about 45 degrees above PQ) to point R (small dot at R), labelled "4 cm" along the segment (text rotated to the slope). Letters: P at the left end of PQ, Q at the right end, R beside the upper end of PR. No angle mark, no arc.

belongs_to: Fig. 8.2: "open up the compass against a ruler (see Fig. 8.2) such that the distance between the tip of the compass and the pencil is 4 cm" and "the point P is called the centre of the circle and the distance between the centre and any point on the circle is called the radius"
description: Fig. 8.2 has two coloured panels side by side. Left panel: a compass (grey legs, black hinge with a nut, pencil fixed in the left leg with its sharp tip pointing down, metal needle on the right leg) standing on a ruler marked in cm with numerals 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 (small marks between the numerals). The pencil tip is exactly at 0 and the needle tip is exactly at 4, i.e. the compass is opened to 4 cm. Right panel: the same compass drawing a circle; the needle stands on a dot labelled "P" with the word "centre" written beside it (to the right); a straight line from P to the circle on the left carries the word "radius" written along it; the pencil tip sits on the circle at the left end of that radius; the circle is drawn as a thin outline around P. Caption "Fig. 8.2" below.

belongs_to: Construct 1. "A Person - How will you draw this?"
description: A simple person made of three parts, all black outlines: a circle (the head) at the top; directly below it a short vertical straight segment (the neck) hanging from the bottom of the circle down to the middle of the top of the body; the body is a shape with two vertical sides (left and right), a horizontal bottom, and a top that is not a straight line but a circular arc that dips down in the middle (curving like a smile, i.e. concave upwards), its two ends at the top of the vertical sides and its lowest point at the middle where the neck touches it. Head diameter is a little less than the body width (about 0.8 of it); the body is about as tall as it is wide and the arc dips by about a fifth of the body width. No labels, no measurements.

belongs_to: "This figure has two components. You might have figured out a way of drawing the first part."
description: The person of A Person split into its two components, side by side. Left component: the head circle with the neck segment hanging below it as a free short vertical line (not attached to anything). Right component: the body, a shape with two vertical sides, a flat bottom and a top that is an arc dipping down in the middle (concave upwards, ends level with the tops of the sides). No labels.

belongs_to: "For drawing the second part, see this." (the challenge: where to place the tip of the compass and the radius for the curve)
description: The body shape of A Person (flat bottom, two vertical sides) with its top curve being drawn by a compass. The curve is a shallow arc dipping down in the middle (concave upwards) and it runs slightly beyond the left and right vertical sides. The compass (grey metal legs, black hinge, orange pencil) is drawn above the body: its needle tip rests above the middle of the arc and its pencil tip is at the right end of the arc, so the arc is a part of a circle whose centre lies above the body. No labels, no measurements.

belongs_to: Construct 2. "Wavy Wave - Construct this."
description: A horizontal straight line (the central line) with two half circles standing on it, joined end to end: the left half of the line carries a half circle bulging UP (above the line), the right half of the line carries a half circle bulging DOWN (below the line). The two half circles have equal radius; the diameter of each is half of the central line, so the left half circle ends where the right one begins, at the middle of the line, and the whole figure looks like a sideways S / sine wave. Both half circles are filled with thin closely spaced vertical lines (about 29 vertical strokes across each, black on white) and have a bold black outline; the central line is bold black. No labels, no measurements.
unclear: Number of hatch lines (about 29 per half circle, counted along one row) is approximate and only decorative.

(the compass opening is unknown). Right: a horizontal line with points A at its left end, X on it about the middle (at the right end of the half circle) and B at its right end. belongs_to: Construct 3. "Eyes - How do you draw these eyes with a compass?"
description: Two identical eyes side by side in one row. Each eye is an almond (lens) shape made of two circular arcs, one bulging up and one bulging down, meeting at pointed corners at the far left and far right; the outline is bold black and the inside is white. In the middle of each eye is a solid black filled oval (the pupil), centred. The right pointed corner of the left eye almost touches the left pointed corner of the right eye (a tiny gap). The two eyes are mirror/identical copies. No labels, no measurements.

belongs_to: Fig. 8.3 (8.2 Squares and Rectangles: "Now, let us look at some basic figures having straight lines in their boundary"); also the figure of Figure it Out Q1 on p.194 ("rectangle and four squares configuration (shown in Fig. 8.3)")

The arrangement is symmetric: the four squares are mirror images of each other across the horizontal and vertical centre lines of the rectangle. All outlines black, no fill, no labels. belongs_to: Figure it Out Q2: "Identify if there are any squares in this collection. Use measurements if needed." (A B C D), with the Think: "reason out ... only by looking at the position of corners in the dot grid"

A: corners (5,1), (9,5), (5,9), (1,5): a tilted square standing on a corner; each side runs 4 columns across and 4 rows up or down, the horizontal and vertical diagonals are both 8 units. B: corners (15,1), (18,5), (15,9), (12,5): a tall diamond; sides go 3 across and 4 down/up (length 5 units each), vertical diagonal 8, horizontal diagonal 6. C: corners (26,1), (31,5), (26,9), (21,5): a wide diamond; sides go 5 across and 4 down/up, horizontal diagonal 10, vertical diagonal 8. D: corners (36,3), (38,4), (36,8), (34,7): a small tilted rectangle; the short sides go 2 across and 1 up/down, the long sides go 2 across and 4 up/down (long side twice the short side). The shapes are separated by empty dot space; the letters sit under each shape at its horizontal centre.
unclear: The dot grid is 40 columns x 11 rows by pixel count; a few dots are hidden by the watermark, so the exact column total may be off by one.

belongs_to: Explore: "constructing a rectangle that can be divided into two identical squares ... One way is to visualise the final figure by drawing a rough diagram of it." (and "A convention is followed to represent equal sides. It is done by putting a | on the line. Refer to the rough figure.")

belongs_to: "As, AB = AF, we need to somehow transfer the length of AF to get the point B ... Observe, how the length of AF is measured using a compass."
